ic_name: NFC / ISO 14443 (NXP AN10833 MIFARE family — subset)
otp_summary: The PICC's UID + ATQA + SAK + ATS are factory-programmed into the IC's OTP region during wafer / package test and are immutable thereafter (with the explicit exception of Random ID (RID) variants where UID1..UID3 are randomised at each Power-on Reset). Together these fields form a deterministic identification fingerprint of the chip family per AN10833. MIFARE-application-layer OTP (e.g. one-time-programmable lock bytes on MIFARE Ultralight pages 2-3, or per-sector PERM lock bits on MIFARE Classic) is above Layer 3 and is documented per family in their respective product datasheets.

otp_registers.name: UID

fields.name: Manufacturer Byte (UID0)
fields.description: ISO 7816-6 manufacturer code (0x04 = NXP, 0x05 = Infineon, 0x07 = STMicro, 0x08 = Random).

fields.name: Serial (UID1..UID3)
fields.description: Per-chip serial — derived from wafer ID + die position.

fields.name: Serial extension (7B UID)
fields.description: Continues UID for double-size UID PICCs.

fields.name: Serial extension (10B UID)
fields.description: Continues UID for triple-size UID PICCs.

otp_registers.exception_random_id: When UID0 = 0x08 (Random ID mode), UID1..UID3 are NOT OTP; they are randomised at each Power-on Reset by an internal RNG.

fields.name: Bit-frame AC bitmap
fields.description: Indicates which bit-frame anti-collision variant the PICC supports.

fields.name: UID not complete flag
fields.description: 1 = Cascade Tag follows in next CL.

fields.name: Proprietary
fields.description: Vendor encoding of family variant + capacity.

otp_registers.name: ATS (Layer 4)
otp_registers.factory_programmed: mostly (chip vendor), but customisable per application

non_otp_card_state: Layer-3-volatile state — current PICC state (IDLE / READY / ACTIVE / HALT / T_CL_ACTIVE), T=CL block-number counter, CID assignment, FSCI / FWI negotiated session, application-layer authentication session keys — all lost when the carrier is removed.
notes: The UID is the primary irreversible identification field. UID0 = 0x04 binds the chip to NXP; the manufacturer byte cannot be altered post-fabrication. For families that adopt RID (Random ID) the host should not use UID1..UID3 for any persistent identification purpose — the appropriate stable identifier is then exposed via GetUID under a T=CL authenticated session. AN10833 explicitly recommends GetVersion (where supported) over ATQA/SAK for exact identification because SAK values may be re-used in future products (note 4).
